scope: Compare Native host opt-level 1 and 0 while extracted Core and other dependencies remain at opt-level 1. This experiment changes only temporary Cargo configuration, not the repository profile.

sources.difference: Measurement notes only; production Core extraction source is identical. Exact revision changes force the real embedded CLI and Native identity to rebuild.

environment.target_isolation: One private persistent target per arm, sequential builds, separate per-arm Kache job runtimes and one bounded shared object store

method: Interleave Native1 A, Native0 A, Native1 B, Native0 B. Build the canonical CLI, package without a second compile, restore and verify both CLI and Native source identities, run all 29 tool-parsing and 33 workflow conformance scenarios, and run the actual Rust prompt-prose scan three times. All commands exited zero; every conformance result had zero failures and skips. Initial target warmth differs, so use the B pair for the warm comparison.
decision: This initial owned-incremental experiment did not justify a profile change alone: the warm build improved by 21.98 seconds while prompt scanning slowed about 41 percent. The subsequent hosted-shaped, non-incremental experiment in bench/hosted-native-opt-level-9112.json measures the full owning audit consumers and records the adoption decision. No ten-minute CI p90 improvement is established here.

evidence.runtime_identity: Restored archive's CLI source_revision and runtime_content_fingerprint.source_revision equal the selected full source SHA, with full and otel enabled and default disabled.
evidence.caveats: Four runs are not a CI cohort. Initial target warmth differs. Kache's forced incremental Native pass-through is absent from its object-event list; Cargo unit timings prove compilation. Other host work may affect wall time. Original temporary Cargo configuration was restored and compared on successful exit.
